until epiphyseal fusion occurs near the end of puberty
Growth failure due to Prader-Willi Syndrome
Short stature associated w/ Turner syndrome

Tx of pts w/ short bowel syndrome dependent on TPN
: peripheral edema, myalgias, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome
: pseudotumor cerebri, progression of scoliosis, edema, hyperglycemia, intracranial HTN (vision changes, HA, N/V), pancreatitis, gynecomastia, nevus growth
•Prader-Willi syndrome: increased risk of asphyxiation in severely obese pts, upper airway obstruction or sleep apnea
•Turner syndrome: increased risk of otitis media
: approved for tx of severe IGF deficiency that is not responsive to hGH
: epiphyseal fusion has already occurred, existing cancer, other causes of growth failure
: hypoglycemia, intracranial HTN, asymptomatic elevation of liver enzymes, enlarged tonsils, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, worsened scoliosis
: inhibits release of GH, TSH, glucagon, insulin, and gastrin
Symptom control in pts w/ metastatic carcinoid tumors
Diarrhea associated w/ vasoactive intestinal peptide-secreting tumors (VIPomas)
: GI (N/V, cramps, flatulence, steatorrhea), biliary sludge, gallstones (after 6mo of use), sinus bradycardia, conduction disturbances
: long-term treatment of acromegaly that cannot be treated w/ or is unresponsive to radiation or surgery
: diarrhea, gallbladder problems, abdominal pain, nausea, injection site reactions

: polyethylene glycol (PEG) derivative of a mutant rhGH with altered GH receptor binding sites (one site has increased receptor affinity, and the other site has decreased affinity); allows for GH receptor dimerization (initial binding step), but blocks conformational changes needed for signal transduction; therefore, a GH receptor antagonist
: treatment of acromegaly in pts who have not responded adequately to surgery, radiation therapy, or other medical therapies or would not be appropriate candidates for these therapies
: has high affinity for both V1A and V2 receptors; inhibits V2 receptors and causes aquaresis (excretion of free water)
: tx of euvolemic hyponatremia in hospitalized pts
: hypovolemic hyponatremia, concurrent use w/ potent CYP3A inhibitors, anuric pts
: tx of pts w/ “clinically significant” hypervolemic or euvolemic hyponatremia; used in HF, cirrhosis, & SIADH

: need urgent intervention to increase serum sodium, unable to sense or respond appropriately to thirst, hypovolemic hyponatremia, concurrent use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, not forming/excreting urine
: therapy should begin or resume only in a hospital where sodium concentration can be closely monitored
